subject: Radioactivity
concept: Unstable nuclei transform by alpha, beta, or gamma decay: alpha sheds 2 protons and 2 neutrons, beta converts a neutron into a proton, gamma releases energy with no particle change.

formulas.when_to_use: Heavy unstable nuclei shedding mass: mass number drops by 4, atomic number by 2.
formulas.derivation: Nucleon and charge conservation: 4 nucleons and 2 protons leave with the alpha particle.

formulas.when_to_use: Neutron-rich nuclei: mass number unchanged, atomic number rises by 1.
formulas.derivation: Weak interaction converts a neutron; charge balances via the emitted electron.

formulas.when_to_use: Excited nucleus shedding energy: A and Z both unchanged.
formulas.derivation: Energy conservation only — no nucleons move.

examples.text: Uranium-238 (Z = 92) alpha-decays: A 238 → 234, Z 92 → 90, giving Thorium-234.
Carbon-14 (Z = 6) beta-decays: A stays 14, Z rises to 7, giving Nitrogen-14.

practice.prompt: Uranium-238 alpha-decays. Find the mass number A of the new nucleus.
Uranium-238 (Z = 92) alpha-decays. Find the atomic number Z of the new nucleus.
Carbon-14 (Z = 6) beta-decays. Find the atomic number Z of the new nucleus.
An alpha particle is emitted. What is its mass number?
Polonium-218 (Z = 84) alpha-decays twice in a row. Find the final atomic number Z.
